Does it make sence to create a SDK or wheel from DataQ?
If yes what is the feasibility?
I'll ground this in the repo before answering: packaging metadata, the integrations folder, ADR 0031, and whether an OpenAPI client was ever discussed.

CLAUDE.md:357:**Next milestone:** **v1.2 Week 1 — decision gates + MCP honesty burn-down (due 2026-08-28)** — #590/#588 are the user's keep-or-teardown decisions (~08-25 revisit; ask, never decide unilaterally), plus #1392/#1257 and the six MCP honesty follow-ups. Full plan in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md). *(v1.1 close-out record follows.)* The `v1.1 Week 7 — stretch (backlog burn-down)` milestone **CLOSED 2026-08-21** at 0 open (exit gate met — every item closed or explicitly rolled with a rationale comment): the final session cleared **#1407** (compose Redis → loopback, plus the marquez/jaeger siblings review caught, #1502), **#1408** (backend image runs as uid 10001, beat's schedule shelve moved to the temp dir so the now-read-only CWD can't crash it — live-verified in the built image, #1503), **#1409** (dead `suite_authz._is_workspace_admin` deleted — the call sites overturned the issue's preferred fix, #1504), **#1410** (checkForm.ts mutation score 67.18%→99.24%, one provably-equivalent survivor; vitest-`toEqual`-swallows-`{key: undefined}` harness lesson, #1506), **#1452** (compliance G6 artifacts under `docs/site/compliance/` — sub-processor disclosure, DPIA input sheet, breach runbook, counsel-gated DPA/BAA drafts, #1507), and **#1412** verified-benign (the "inert" `target_override` never existed — Pydantic `extra='ignore'` swallowed an invented key; residual filed as #1505). Rolled to `v1.1 Backlog` with rationale: #432/#1460 (design conversation first), #505 (**GCP-only now** — AWS shipped), #466/#244 (deferred-by-design), and **#590/#588 — the Azure/Snowflake keep-or-teardown decision gates, owed the user's ~2026-08-25 revisit; ask before touching them.** Earlier the same cycle: W6 closed 2026-08-15, retro merged, **`v1.1.0` tagged** (`b8d8278b`); next-cycle planning input = [docs/retro-v1.1.md](docs/retro-v1.1.md) + the open follow-up graph + [context/post-v1-roadmap.md](context/post-v1-roadmap.md). **Unplanned, user-directed, shipped 2026-08-01/03 — the ADR-0032 email OTP sign-in track, picked up from the `v1.1 Backlog` beside W6 (umbrella [#738](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/738), now closed):** the third authenticator (`bypass · otp · oidc`, `dq_sess_` cookie sessions, mandatory signup allowlist, fail-closed) landed as **11 PRs** across all seven design slices + all five review findings, **COMPLETE 2026-08-02** — pre-implementation recon found the stated hard prerequisite (#725 rate limiting) hadn't actually covered the auth-endpoint class, so an `auth` limiter class + per-email counters shipped first ([#1129](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1129)); then the nullable-`aad_object_id` + unique-lower-email identity migration ([#1131](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1131)); OTP backend core — `sessions`/`otp_codes`, mailer, request/verify/logout ([#1134](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1134)); the frontend two-step sign-in + HttpOnly cookie + server-side revocation, plus a new fully-local `frontend/e2e-otp/` lane ([#1148](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1148)); the SMTP pre-flight test endpoint ([#1143](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1143)); and `/mcp` in otp-only mode, which review found was silently unmounted — fixed with one `mcp_auth_mode()` ladder mirroring the REST gate exactly, so a cookie session still can't reach `/mcp` and only a PAT (`dq_live_…`) can ([#1151](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1151)). **Follow-up wave, CLOSED 2026-08-02/03, +4 PRs:** first-login profile completion for OTP-provisioned users — `PATCH /me` `display_name` + a skippable prompt, closing [#1139](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1139) ([#1153](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1153)); a latency floor on `otp/verify` closing the narrower enumeration channel [#1141](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1141) left open after the request-side floor ([#1154](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1154)); SMTP TLS mode + private-CA bundle for the mailer, closing [#1146](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1146) ([#1155](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1155)); and a per-admin throttle on the SMTP pre-flight endpoint, closing [#1147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1147) ([#1156](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1156)). **Then, unplanned again — both local/eval compose stacks flipped to OTP-by-default** ([#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150), [#1159](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1159)): a bundled **Mailpit** mail catcher (MIT, pinned `v1.30.6`) at `localhost:8025` removes the SMTP relay that made `otp` unusable as a default, so both stacks now boot into email codes instead of dev-bypass, gated by one switch — `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` set = OTP on, explicitly empty = the dev-bypass downgrade, unset = the stack refuses to start rather than picking for you. `scripts/setup.sh` asks for the address; see [Getting started](docs/site/getting-started.md) for the full flow. A same-day test-flake fix ([#1161](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1161)) closed out the track. Full slice-by-slice detail — including the five review-caught defects (an `smtplib.__exit__` that replaces in-flight errors, a compose `environment:`-beats-`env_file:` precedence trap, an ACCESS-EXCLUSIVE-lock doc error, and two more) — is in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) under "Backlog track — ADR 0032 email OTP sign-in". **v1.1 Week 5 — `anomaly` monitor kind + metric trends — CLOSED 2026-08-01, 8/8, a week early:** one orchestrated batch, 10 PRs [#1113](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1113)–[#1122](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1122) — threshold-ordering validation (#568, #1113, closing a `schema_drift` dry-run bypass the review found); the results runs-fetch dedupe + shared date-window presets (#349, #1114, fixing a background-poll-wipes-the-tab bug along the way); an explicit failing-sample redaction state (#424, #1115 — full/partial/none/null, computed read-time via a `_RedactionTracker` so old rows get the correct label for free); Test Connection for unsaved connection drafts (#351, #1116 — `POST /connections/test`, structurally cannot persist; review also surfaced the `*_secret_name` SSRF/exfiltration class on the same auth gate, filed [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118), mitigation deferred to RBAC #740–#744); the **`anomaly` monitor kind itself** (#593, #1117 backend + #1119 authoring UI) — rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality over `metric_value` history, reusing the existing `monitor_baselines` table (no migration), `skip` on cold start, dimension deliberately underivable → NULL (ADR 0038); the per-check metric trend view (#594, #1121) with threshold bands plus a second anomaly-baseline panel, seasonality-aware; check-version restore (#283, #1120), minting a new version rather than delegating to the PATCH-semantics `update_check`; and a zero-dependency PDF report export of a run (#345, #1122). **Live-verified 2026-08-01 against both live warehouses** (the #953 rule — for anything crossing a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence): Snowflake `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` row_count=34680.0 + freshness `ORDER_TS`=132.28h; Unity Catalog `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment` row_count=180.0 + freshness `scored_at`=132.48h — z-scores computed cleanly over both. Every PR carried the mandated `/code-review` agent flow; 15+ real defects were caught pre-merge, including two concurrency bugs (a baseline-UPDATE lost-update race, a stale "Connected" badge) and two honesty-of-display bugs (an under-reported redaction state, a threshold-band caption overclaiming below 2 eligible points); the one deferred finding is #1118 above. **Unplanned, shipped + live-verified 2026-07-28/29 — three batches in one orchestrated session (#1096–#1112, 10 PRs):** Batch 2 reliability (beat **crontabs** #1099 — a 24h interval never fires under embedded beat; **staleness signals** #1100 — stale-lineage surface + de-configured-pull purge + the API-side workspace dead-poll alert on the new `workspace_health` table) and Batches 3+4 assets/lineage (**ADR [0040](docs/site/adr/0040-warehouse-inventory-sync-table-enumeration-seam.md)** — the table-enumeration seam + opt-in per-connection **inventory sync** #1103, so a table with no suite/run/edge is visible-unmonitored instead of invisible (the prod `reference`-schema report); asset **paging + honest truncation** #1105; S3-compatible **endpoint identity** #1106; **GET_LINEAGE per-seed traversal + Snowpark scratch stitching** #1110 — prod's Snowflake lineage lifted from view-level to full tier, live-verified). The recurring lesson bit twice more (#1112): mocked tests stayed green through **two stacked driver-boundary crashes** in one SQL literal (pyformat `%`, then Snowflake's own string parser eating `ESCAPE '\'`) — for warehouse SQL, run the exact statement live before push. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — IaC CLI moved Terraform → OpenTofu (ADR 0024 amendment):** Terraform has been BUSL-1.1 since v1.6 and was the one source-available binary still touching a project ADR 0031 puts on record as MIT-distributed. **Nothing was in violation** — rule 40 governs the dependency tree (what DataQ *ships*) and the CLI never enters an image — so this is coherence, not compliance; the timing argument is #505, since converting one Azure stack is contained and converting three is not. **The acceptance bar was equivalence, not a clean plan**, because the stack already carries pre-existing drift (#1086 — prod's ADR-0034 lineage env vars are absent from `containerapps.tf`, so an apply would DELETE them; the rendered plan hides this behind a positional `env` shuffle and only `show -json` reveals it): both CLIs were run against live Azure, plans exported with `-out`, rendered via `show -json`, and the normalized `resource_changes` diffed — **byte-for-byte identical** (40 changes, `no-op=38 update=2`), provider versions preserved exactly, only the registry host + hashes moved. The *rendered* text plans DO differ (branding, refresh ordering, column alignment, hidden-attribute counts), which is why eyeballing them would not have settled it. State, providers, and the `deploy/terraform/<cloud>/` path are unchanged — `terraform {}` is OpenTofu's own block name. Harness stack converted in the same pass, **plan-only** (a blanket harness apply arms ADF triggers). The swap is **convention, not enforcement** — nothing is OpenTofu-exclusive yet, which is what keeps it reversible; the `encryption {}` follow-up is the one-way door and is deliberately separate. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — S3-compatible endpoints (#1063/#1065):** optional `endpoint_url` + `addressing_style` on the `s3` datasource **and** the `dbt` provider, via one shared `core/s3_endpoint.py`; unlocks MinIO / Ceph / R2 / Wasabi / Backblaze. `auto` → **path** addressing when an endpoint is set is load-bearing (MinIO serves the bucket in the path only, so boto3's virtual-host default fails every read), and `endpoint_url` rejects an embedded credential per the #754/#826 rule. **Live-proven against MinIO** — suite 4/4 over 643 real rows, arrival-time freshness read off `LastModified` — because a non-AWS server is a different implementation and those values cross a driver boundary. It arose from an **Azure-free harness readiness exercise** (local Airflow + MinIO landing zone, all flows green incl. a live Snowflake load; Azure untouched, all five harness apps stayed `Stopped`), whose Snowflake half also produced a standing rule: **nothing in the harness may require a commercial licence** — stricter than rule 40, which governs only what DataQ *ships* — after LocalStack for Snowflake was evaluated and rejected (no community tier; image exits 55). fakesnow (Apache-2.0) is the stand-in, and probing it with DataQ's real code paths found **#1067**: a Snowflake connection with no Role tests green (the test is GX-free) and fails every suite run, since GX requires a `role` query param. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). Follow-ups #1064/#1066. **The four open ADR-0039 follow-ups were then closed the same day (#1069/#1070/#1071):** GHCR `:latest` now republishes on merge (the eval compose is fetched from `main` while the image moved only on dispatch — verified live); the pooled secret-store clients are released on cache reset, with the AKV **credential** closed alongside the client since they hold separate transport sessions; an **orphan-secret sweep** that reports by default and purges only when configured, because what it deletes is a live warehouse credential; and **AppRole auth** (ADR 0039 phase 2) with proactive renewal and one re-login on 403, so a revoked token self-heals instead of 403ing until restart. Two lessons worth carrying: the sweep's ownership registry was wrong **twice** (Slack and Teams are separate refs on one row; `*_secret_name` keys live in JSONB) and its introspection guard was a **tautology** — it iterated the models already registered, so a new model was invisible to it; and #435 was assessed and left open with a corrected AC, since Azure CMK is **creation-time-only** and our IaC stack does not own the Postgres server. **Also unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — the secret-store seam (ADR [0039](docs/site/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md), #1056/#1061):** a fourth `SecretStore` speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API, not a vendor SDK**, so one mode serves OpenBao / Vault Community / Enterprise / HCP — this closes the last seam where Azure was the only production implementation, which #505 (AWS/GCP IaC) would have walked straight into. **OpenBao** (MPL-2.0) is shipped and pinned; Vault Community is BUSL-1.1 and therefore rule-40-forbidden as a *distributed* component, supported only as a target. `SECRET_STORE=openbao` **replaces `redis`** — the plaintext store was the configured default of the published eval stack, i.e. evaluators were putting real warehouse credentials into an unencrypted key-value store. **Redis stays** (Celery broker + ADR 0035 rate limits). Two defects the review caught are worth carrying forward: **an outage must never be reportable as a state** — every caller branches on the exception TYPE and none reads the message, so folding "vault sealed" into `SecretNotFoundError` made an admin page render "not set" and silently skipped alert delivery (`AzureKeyVaultStore` had shipped that since Week 2); and a **`Settings` validator now fails a bad secret-store config at boot**, because the store built lazily and would otherwise die mid-run in a worker. Prod's 13 `conn-*` Key Vault keys were also renamed to one readable convention (`conn-<type>-<qualifier>-<env>-<shortid>`) — copy → read-back verify → repoint → re-test → purge, piloted on one connection first, 11/11 re-verified, and both Airflow connections verified on Key Vault **and** OpenBao. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **DEPLOYED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-19** (then `dff6d958`; prod redeployed to `c401572d` 2026-07-26; prod redeployed again to `bb40f0b7` 2026-08-03 — all three Container Apps (api/worker/frontend) rolled via the Deploy workflow ([run 30789647178](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/30789647178)), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean on the new revision); **prod redeployed to `7018d772` 2026-08-08** — the 2026-08-08 session's eleven merges (#1185/#1188–#1192/#1194/#1198/#1201/#1204 — six-issue fix batch incl. the UC custom-SQL fix, identifier-column display, batch-target UI) rolled via [run 31261342996](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31261342996), migrate no-op (no schema change), full smoke green + a UC suite run 7/7 on the new revisions — see below): the W4 work is on prod and exercised against real datasources. **Prod redeployed to `f637a18e` 2026-08-09** — a full real-user pre-deploy QA pass (2 fresh OTP users, all 4 datasource types, deliberate PASS/FAIL/ERROR + edge-case scenarios via Playwright, no DB shortcuts) found and fixed a live, pre-existing production defect: **#1273** — `decimal.Decimal` values in a legitimately-failed Snowflake/UC NUMERIC-column check crashed the entire result's JSONB insert (`sanitize_json` had no `Decimal` branch), silently discarding the run's results; a passing check on the same column never surfaces the bug, which is why it went unnoticed since `jsonsafe.py` shipped. Fixed in [#1276](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1276) mirroring the file's existing numpy/pandas coercion pattern; mutation-verified regression tests + a live pre/post-fix repro against real Snowflake data. Two more findings filed, both non-blocking: [#1274](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1274) (Iceberg over S3-compatible storage — pyarrow's own S3 client rejects credentials boto3 accepts; scoped to non-ADLS Iceberg backends, likely not this deployment) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation warnings, cosmetic). Also attempted to resolve the user-reported "columns still stretched" report — **that diagnosis was wrong and is corrected below** ([#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282)): the claim recorded here was that [#1184](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1184)'s own fix was already live and only [#1208](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1208) (the RunDetail "Observed" column) was undeployed. Both halves were false. The user re-reported the stretched columns against this very deploy, and pulling the live prod chunks settled it: **both fixes were in the shipped bundle and neither had ever worked, in any environment.** Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `width: max-content` on the `<table>`; an intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its content, neutering `table-layout: fixed` and demoting the `<colgroup>` width to a non-binding hint — so a column's `width` + `ellipsis` are **inert**, and a long ADF error rendered ~1917px wide against a declared 260px. The covering test asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — true, and meaningless, because jsdom performs no layout. Fixed by bounding the **inner element** (`boundedTextStyle`) rather than the column, with the regression assertion moved to Playwright where widths can actually be measured. **Standing practice this produced: "merged" is not "deployed", and "deployed" is not "works" — verify a fix against the running artifact AND against observed behavior before reporting it as done.** Rolled via [run 31342076551](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31342076551), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, `/docs` serves the SPA shell not Swagger, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean, Key Vault secret store initialized on the new revision) — **plus a live suite run** ("Snowflake — Orders (all paths)", 7 checks, 6 pass/1 fail/1 skip, `succeeded`) confirming the #1273 fix holds against real prod data. **Prod redeployed twice more the same day — to `77068358`, then to `eba60b4d` (current)** ([run 31347217502](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31347217502), [run 31350288817](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31350288817)); both migrate jobs no-op (zero migration files in either delta), both smokes green, and the fixes **verified in the running artifact and in the browser**, not merely merged: the deployed chunk `ellipsisColumn-*.js` carries `boundedTextStyle`, and the Failure-reason cell that had rendered ~1917px now measures 260px with 3423px of content clipped, Observed 220px, the pipeline table 1379px instead of 2969px. The second roll carried two post-deploy-smoke findings from the first: **#1286** (the fix’s own regression — a 150px bound wrapped the copy button and grew every pipeline-runs row 56px→77px; measured the threshold on live prod and shipped 120) and **#1285** (pre-existing — orchestration poll failures were classified through the datasource message set, so both Airflow connections said “missing warehouse or role … check the suite’s run target” while the harness Airflow app was simply Stopped; an orchestration connection has none of those four things). Both confirmed live afterwards: 20/20 Provider-run cells clipped at 120px with a uniform 56px row height, and the 02:51Z poll wrote the new orchestration-shaped reason. A live suite run on each revision (8 checks) confirmed the worker path against real Snowflake. **Verification lesson from this session, now standing practice: “merged” is not “deployed”, and “deployed” is not “works” — a stale-looking grep in the wrong chunk nearly produced a second wrong answer, and the first poll after the roll still showed the old message because the draining revision served it.** Orchestration (Airflow trigger → poll → dispatch) was also verified end-to-end in the local harness this session, after fixing a stale `DATAQ_LOADER`-scoped Snowflake credential in the harness's own (untracked, separate-repo) local stack — see [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **ADLS** — volume read 643 rows off the resolved batch and arrival-time freshness reported 531.8h from the blob's last-modified: the harness genuinely stopped producing, which is precisely the incident #520 exists to catch and which an in-file MAX cannot see. **Snowflake** — `order_ts` (lower-case, emitted unquoted so the warehouse folds it) and `ORDER_TS` (upper-case, now quoted) returned **identical** timestamps, proving #937 both fixes mixed case and preserves the fold; volume over 32,840 real rows. **Unity Catalog** — freshness works **for the first time ever** (239.06h, lower/UPPER identical, confirming the backtick dialect). The dimension backfill (#952) classified **all 30 real prod checks, zero unclassified**, and real asset scorecards show genuine signal. **Live testing found a bug three green suites could not: UC freshness had NEVER worked** (#953) — the Databricks connector returns a TIMESTAMP's MAX as a **str** and the age math accepted only datetime/date, so a datasource the feature matrix marks ✅ produced no reading since #426. No unit test could see it: the type comes from the **driver**, and every fixture hands in a real datetime — the same fixture-encodes-our-model shape as #823 and the #520 Parquet bug. **Lesson: for anything whose type or value crosses a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence.** Also filed [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954): two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a **datasource** connection with a dead credential has no visible state until a run fails — I had to read worker logs to find out why, since #839's health signal covers only *orchestration* connections. Yes for a thin **client SDK**, no for a **library wheel of the backend**. Grounded in the repo as it stands today:

**What exists**
- 110 versioned REST routes under `/api/v1`, Pydantic-typed, with a Swagger/OpenAPI spec that was already audited for completeness and error shape (#465).
- PATs (`dq_live_`) already give headless clients a stable bearer auth path. The AWS demo PATs in SSM prove the flow works outside a browser.
- `backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py` is already a hand-rolled HTTP client in bearer mode. That is the SDK, unpackaged.
- No Python packaging metadata anywhere. The root `pyproject.toml` only configures Black/Ruff/mypy. CLAUDE.md §3 explicitly names "an auto-generated OpenAPI client" as the one thing that would justify a `packages/` directory.

**Option 1: `dataq-client` Python wheel generated from the OpenAPI spec. Recommended.**
- Feasibility: high, roughly one to two days. Export the spec via `app.openapi()` in CI, generate with `openapi-python-client` (MIT, rule-40 clean), add a small hand-written layer on top: PAT auth, `trigger_run` + `wait_for_run` polling, raise on `error`/`failed`.
- Who uses it: CI/CD pipelines gating a deploy on a suite result (the consumer side of #1651 without needing the ADR), notebooks, Airflow tasks that want more than the callback snippet, and anyone scripting suite import/export.
- Guardrail needed: a CI contract test that regenerates from the current spec and fails on drift, otherwise the published wheel silently ages the way the MCP docstrings did. Version the wheel with the app, not independently.
- Watch-outs from past findings: the `results_final`-style honesty fields that MCP carries do not all exist on REST, so a `wait_for_run` helper must read run status, not check counts. Pydantic `extra='ignore'` (#1412) means a typo'd field in a client call is swallowed server-side; the generated typed models fix that for free.

**Option 2: `dataq-integrations` wheel for the Airflow and dbt callbacks. Not worth it.**
Both snippets are deliberately stdlib-only single files so they drop into any Airflow image without a pip install. A wheel adds a dependency and a release cadence for zero code gain.

**Option 3: `dataq-core` engine as an importable library. No.**
`backend/app` is an application, not a library: runners resolve through `Settings`, the SQLAlchemy session, the `SecretStore` seam and Celery; 39 pinned runtime deps including GX, Snowflake, Databricks and pyiceberg. Extracting `datasources/` + `gx_runner` would be a large refactor with no consumer asking for it, and MCP already covers "programmatic DataQ" for AI clients.

**Timing.** Not W5 (DMF + notification channels). It fits W7 feature burn-down or the v1.3 roadmap in `context/roadmap-v1.2-v1.3.md`. I can file the issue for Option 1 with the scope above if you want it on the board.

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/35b1af29-9edc-49a2-9b7d-86cf05a9416e/scratchpad/issue.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

Publish a thin Python client SDK (`dataq-client`) generated from DataQ's own OpenAPI spec, with a small hand-written convenience layer on top. **Parked for v1.3** (decision 2026-09-02) — roadmap Track 2, beside #1705 (API compatibility policy), which is its prerequisite.

**Explicitly NOT in scope** (assessed and rejected 2026-09-02, so it isn't re-litigated):
- A library wheel of `backend/app` (`dataq-core`). It is an application, not a library — runners resolve through `Settings`, the SQLAlchemy session, the `SecretStore` seam and Celery; 39 pinned runtime deps (GX, Snowflake, Databricks, pyiceberg). Extracting `datasources/` + `gx_runner` is a large refactor with no consumer asking for it, and MCP already covers programmatic access for AI clients.
- A `dataq-integrations` wheel for the Airflow/dbt callbacks. Both are deliberately stdlib-only single files so they drop into any scheduler image without a pip install; a wheel adds a dependency and a release cadence for zero code gain.

## Why

- 110 versioned routes under `/api/v1`, Pydantic-typed, with an OpenAPI spec already audited for completeness + error shape (#465). PATs (`dq_live_`) already give headless clients a stable bearer path (the AWS demo PATs in SSM prove it end-to-end).
- `backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py` is already a hand-rolled HTTP client in bearer mode — the SDK exists, unpackaged.
- CLAUDE.md §3 names "an auto-generated OpenAPI client" as the one thing that justifies a `packages/` directory.
- Consumers: CI/CD pipelines gating a deploy on a suite result (the *consumer* side of #1651 without needing its ADR), notebooks, Airflow tasks wanting more than the callback snippet, scripted suite export/import.

## Scope

1. **Spec export in CI** — `app.openapi()` dumped to a checked artifact (not hand-maintained).
2. **Generated client** — `openapi-python-client` (MIT; rule-40 / ADR 0031 clean) into `packages/dataq-client/`. Typed models for every request/response.
3. **Convenience layer (hand-written, small)** — `DataQClient(base_url, pat)`; `trigger_run(suite_id)`; `wait_for_run(run_id, timeout)` that polls **run status** and raises on `error`/`failed`; suite export/import helpers.
4. **Versioning** — the wheel version tracks the app version (`v1.x.y`), never independent. Published to PyPI on tag.
5. **Docs** — one page under `docs/site/` (+ nav) with the CI-gate example; feature-matrix row.

## Guardrails (non-negotiable, from prior findings)

- **Drift contract test in CI**: regenerate from the current spec and fail on any diff against the committed client. Without it the published wheel silently ages, exactly the way the MCP docstrings did when a neighbour changed (#1444 lesson).
- **`wait_for_run` must read run status, not check counts.** The `results_final`-style honesty fields MCP carries do not all exist on REST; a mid-run `3/3, worst_severity: null` is the "nothing failed" shape (Tier-1 MCP finding).
- **Typed models are the fix for `extra='ignore'`** (#1412 class): today a typo'd field in a raw HTTP call is swallowed server-side; the generated models make it a client-side error.
- **Decimal / JSONB shapes**: NUMERIC thresholds reach JSON as `Decimal` on some surfaces (#1273 / `export_suite` finding) — verify the generated models round-trip export→import against a real suite, not a fixture.
- **No credential in the package, ever** — PAT is a constructor argument / env var; no `.env` reading, no keyring.
- **Never publish the client from a fork/branch build**: PyPI publish only from the release tag workflow with OIDC trusted publishing (no long-lived PyPI token in secrets).
- **License**: MIT, matching ADR 0031; `openapi-python-client` output has no copyleft transitive deps (verify with `pip-audit` + a licence check in the package's own CI).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pip install dataq-client` → CI-gate example runs against a live deployment with a PAT (trigger → wait → non-zero exit on failure), verified on Azure **and** AWS (per-cloud verify, not inferred from the workflow exit code).
- [ ] Drift test proven able to FAIL (mutation-check: change one route's response model, watch CI go red).
- [ ] Export→import round-trip through the SDK on a real suite with NUMERIC thresholds.
- [ ] `docs/site/` page published; changelog entry.

## Effort

~1–2 days once #1705 (compatibility policy) is decided. Do **not** pull into v1.2 W5–W8.
EOF
